Sandwich Franchise Acquires Technology Company

GROVE CITY (February 27)—Lunch Hut, the national restaurant franchise known for serving farm-to-table sandwiches, has acquired My Handy Chef, a technology company that manufactures a line of robots that can perform basic kitchen tasks. My Handy Chef cofounder Ryan Boone has joined Lunch Hut's corporate office as an innovation strategist, bringing with him a team of talented engineers and designers.

The robots are skilled in mixing ingredients for sauces and spreads as well as peeling and chopping vegetables.

With the acquisition of My Handy Chef, Lunch Hut's leadership team is excited to make progress toward automating the production of such signature dishes as their famous Pasta with Farm Greens Pesto and Spicy Egg Salad.

"At its best, technology facilitates smoother human interactions, and I believe this development will help us to do an even better job of attending to our customers' needs," said Eva Griffin, Lunch Hut's longtime CEO. Lunch Hut has always been known for the personable service of its staff members, who assemble each custom sandwich order by hand.

The Southern Cultural League is proud to present our first annual storytelling event, hosted by the Sydney Public Library. Cassie Gates, our director, has booked four speakers who are sure to inspire you with innovative ways to incorporate storytelling into your lives and classrooms.

8:00-9:45 A.M. Introduction: The Power of Story
Local storyteller Rarriwuy Henry sets a shining example as she spins a delightful tale that demonstrates how we, as storytellers, can spread the joy of this ancient tradition.

Family stories—we all have them, but how do we tell them? Liam Murphy, a storyteller from Melbourne, shares tips for turning precious memories into tales that can be passed down through generations.

There's something about rhythm and rhyme that touches our souls and stays in our minds. Poet Janna Gibson explains how we can incorporate elements of verse into our stories to make them more memorable.

3:00-4:45 P.M. From Books to Oral Tales
Maybe you write books. Maybe you read them. But how do we make the stories within them come alive to a listening audience? Author Ann Sparks shares her secrets for telling written stories in captivating ways.

KIMBERLEY CONSULTING GEOENGINEERS

Resource Assessment
Client: Springbok Concrete Suppliers LLC
Property examined: Bhule Gravel Quarry
Purpose: To determine how long Springbok Concrete Suppliers LLC can continue mining the Bhule Gravel Quarry pits for gravel
Dates: 15-19 July

Summary of main findings of the assessment team: — [1] —. We examined the availability of high-quality gravel in and around the two main quarry pits at Bhule Gravel Quarry. First, we took samples from several different locations around the North Quarry pit. After analyzing the samples, we determined that there is very little mineable gravel left in or around the North Quarry pit. — [2] —. Therefore, we recommend ending this operation within the next year. In addition, it is not cost-effective to mine the gravel at the North Quarry pit even though it is closer to the processing plant than the South Quarry pit is.

In contrast, there are extensive amounts of gravel still to be mined in the South Quarry pit. The samples we retrieved by drilling indicate that the mineable gravel deposits extend 800 metres south of the pit and to a depth of 15 metres. If gravel continues to be mined at the current rate, we estimate that the mining operation at the South Quarry pit can be sustained for another three years. — [3] —. The cost of the operation will gradually increase because it will be necessary to dig deeper. Nevertheless, we believe the operation will remain profitable. — [4] —.

Assessment prepared by: Gertruida Botha and Moeketsi Mosala

A Better Way to Watch Whales

QUEBEC CITY (30 May)—A new local firm, Saguenay Eco-Adventure (SEA), will offer whale-watching tours in the St. Lawrence River beginning in July.

Tour participants will travel in comfortable charter buses from Quebec City to the boat's departure point on the St. Lawrence River.

The bus trip is a scenic drive of just under three hours and includes a stop at Montmorency Falls, a popular tourist site.

Half-day cruises are available on either a large boat with a spacious deck or a small boat offering a more intimate experience.

Although whales are the main focus, many different types of marine mammals and birds are also likely to be seen in the area. Knowledgeable tour guides will provide expert commentary and help visitors spot wildlife.

One feature sets these tours apart. SEA is one of the few whale-watching tour companies that rely on renewable energy sources. SEA's buses and boats are powered by biodiesel, and the larger boats are equipped with solar panels to power their electrical equipment.

Visit saguenayecoadventure.ca for more details.

documents.label: review
documents.text:
Review of Saguenay Eco-Adventure's Whale-Watching Tour

10 July—I recently took an excursion with Saguenay Eco-Adventure (SEA). Although it was foggy and rainy when we boarded our boat, the fog cleared after an hour, and the visibility was excellent the rest of the day. We saw numerous whales, seals, and other wildlife. The boat was big and roomy, and our tour guide, Pierre, was excellent. He gave the tour in both French and English, seamlessly alternating between the two languages. My only disappointment was the bus ride to the boat launch site. The bus driver was instructed not to stop at Montmorency Falls because there was unusually heavy traffic in the area, and SEA did not want us to miss our boat departure. I wanted to see the falls, but I was thankful we arrived at the launch site on time.

—Otto Pfeiffer

The Golden Star Book Awards
Open for Submissions May 12 to July 16

Every August, the Wilbury Writers League honors four members of our group with a Golden Star Book Award. These awards represent literary excellence in an unpublished fiction manuscript that has not yet been submitted to an agent. The winners will be awarded in each of the categories listed below. They will be recognized on our Web site and will meet with a literary agent currently seeking to represent new and upcoming authors.

Entry Fee per Category $60

Contemporary | Character-driven novel with a strong female protagonist
Historical | Set in the nineteenth century or earlier
Mystery and Detective | Plot-driven novel told from a first-person perspective
Children and Young Adult | Realistic fiction with human protagonists

You can submit manuscripts in multiple categories, but each requires a separate entry fee. Submit your work at www.wilburywritersleague.org/gsba.

Lewis Contemporary Art Museum (LCAM) Lecture Series

LCAM is hosting a lecture series in June to celebrate its tenth anniversary. Admission is free for LCAM members and $10 per lecture for the general public. Space is limited, so register early. Walk-ins are allowed if space permits. All lectures begin at 8:00 P.M. and are held in the LCAM auditorium.

June 3-Looking at Plebani
Dr. Juan Rodriguez, a professor at Northern University, will explore the textile works of Smithtown's most prolific artist, Marcia Plebani. He will discuss Plebani's most important works, including her Watching Birds series.

June 10-Jerry Wadley's Turning Points
LCAM artistic director Hyejeong Kim will examine how Jerry Wadley's style evolved over his 70-year career. Dr. Kim will focus on how Mr. Wadley's sculptures came to capture the beauty and mystery of ordinary people.

June 17-Our Views
Dr. Ayano Goto, a professor at Rampel University, will discuss a selection of landscape paintings by Ara Na, focusing on why and how Na chooses which landscapes to paint.

June 24-The Photographs of Lily Losaru
LCAM associate curator Emilio Loria will delve into Lily Losaru's photography. He will show how Ms. Losaru uses portrait photography to reflect the interests and personalities of her subjects.
